annotation.summary_en: A colonel scolds a lower-ranking officer for being too direct with punishments, only to be outsmarted by a clever soldier when he tries to demonstrate a more 'subtle' method.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a military compound where a colonel spots a lower-ranking officer, Grigoryan, shouting orders at a soldier to repeatedly lie down and stand up. The colonel intervenes, arguing that such blunt punishment is uncivilized. He explains that one should punish a soldier subtly so they don't even realize it is happening. His proposed method involves sending a soldier for water and repeatedly finding faults with the container, temperature, or source to keep them running back and forth. To prove his point, the colonel calls over Private Kirakosyan and orders him to get water. However, the clever soldier, anticipating the trap, asks all the clarifying questions at once: should it be in a metal or glass cup, cold or warm, and from the tap or a bottle? Realizing his psychological tactic has failed, the frustrated colonel reverts to the direct method he originally criticized, screaming at the soldier to start doing push-ups.
catchphrases: շարքային Կիրակոսյան հլը վազելով գնա ջուր բեր խմեմ պարոն Գնդապետ իսկ երկաթից բաժակով բերեմ թե ապակուց ապակուց իսկ սառը թե գոլ գոլ իսկ ջուրը կռանթից լցնեմ թե շշից  իիի պառռռռկել
